title: Tudok, Tudsz, Tud – Saying What You're Able To Do

sections.title: A verb that conjugates, unlike kell
sections.content: tud ("to be able to, to know how to") combines with an infinitive just like kell does — Tudok úszni ("I can swim") — but unlike kell and kellene, tud is a completely regular verb and conjugates for every person: tudok, tudsz, tud, tudunk, tudtok, tudnak. That's the key difference between the two kinds of "can/should" words in this unit: kellene talks about what's advisable for anyone, while tud talks about what a specific person is actually capable of.

items.spanish: Nem tudok aludni, mert fáj a fejem.
items.english: I can't sleep because my head hurts.

items.spanish: Nem tud sportolni, mert fáj a lába.
items.english: He/she can't play sports because his/her leg hurts.

sections.content: Don't confuse tud with kellene: Kellene korán kelni describes good advice ("one should get up early"); Nem tudok korán kelni describes a real limit ("I'm not able to get up early") — one is about what's wise, the other about what's possible for you.
